title: Page Number with Page Change Indicator

illustrates.quote: The numeric and alphabetic numbers must appear on the same braille page.

page.features: New print page (89, alphabetic 'eighty-nine') begins in the middle of this braille page: both the ordinary mid-page page-change indicator and the alphabetic-number line are needed on the same braille page, per 1.14.1.b.

blocks.features: Schematic placeholder for generic body text ('text 444'); no real print excerpt is given -- illustrates alphabetic-page-number placement mechanics directly in braille.

braille.notes: Braille page lines 11-14, verbatim. Line 11: text ending the previous print page. Line 12: the mid-page page-change indicator ending in the numeric page number '#hi' (89). Line 13: the alphabetic page number ('eighty-nine'), preceded by six cells of the page-change-indicator symbol, on the line immediately after the numeric indicator (a new print page begins mid-braille-page, so the alphabetic number does not land on line 1/2 of a fresh page). Line 14 resumes body text.

resolution: Both runs agree on the braille content and on there being no real print excerpt to build from. Emboss has no spelled-out (alphabetic) page-number feature at all (standards-findings.md F-49) -- there is also no real print content behind the placeholder. status: not-representable (limitation: no print given, and F-49).
